compound.name: apigenin
compound.one_liner: Chamomile's benzodiazepine-site flavone (Ki ~4 µM in vitro); anxiolytic in mice, poorly bioavailable in people.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Salvia officinalis L., folium and Salvia officinalis L., aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/150801/2015 (20 Sep 2016). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-salvia-officinalis-l-folium-and-salvia-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: APIGENIN Plant and Shoot, no values. EMA lists apigenin and its glycosides (no individual %).

occurrences.source_citation: Kosakowska O, et al. (2021) Antioxidant and antibacterial activity of essential oils and hydroethanolic extracts of Greek oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. hirtum (Link) Ietswaart) and common oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. vulgare). Molecules 26(4):988
occurrences.note: Reported as glycosides: see apigenin-7-glucoside. KNApSAcK: Apigenin C00003817 listed for Origanum vulgare subsp. hirtum. Paper reports apigenin 7-O-glucoside present in the hirtum extract; free apigenin not separately quantified, so paper-level verification of the aglycone is false.

pharmacology.primary_targets: Benzodiazepine binding site of the GABA-A receptor (flunitrazepam displacement, Ki about 4 µM) [36].
pharmacology.mechanism: Partial ligand at the central benzodiazepine site; anxiolytic in mice without sedation or muscle relaxation, mild sedation only at much higher doses [36, 37]. EMA also cites antispasmodic activity on isolated guinea-pig ileum [10].
pharmacology.functional_notes: The chamomile GAD trials tested a standardised whole-flower extract, not apigenin [57].

compound.absorption_bioavailability: Plant apigenin is mostly glycosides that must be hydrolysed by intestinal or bacterial β-glucosidases; absorbed apigenin is extensively glucuronidated/sulfated and recycled enterohepatically, and plasma levels after parsley were nanomolar; its oral bioavailability is characterised as low [44].

evidence.claim: Apigenin binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors.
Apigenin is anxiolytic in mice without sedation.
evidence.outcome_summary: Increased open-arm time; no myorelaxant or anticonvulsant action at anxiolytic doses.

evidence.claim: Apigenin is spasmolytic on isolated gut tissue.

processing_stability.note: In the flower mainly as apigenin-7-glucoside [10]; free-aglycone solubility not sourced.

compound.teaching_note: A good test of evidence grading: a strong in-vitro and mouse story [36] and a positive human trial of the whole extract [57], but no trial of apigenin itself, and poor bioavailability in between [44].
gaps: No human trial of isolated apigenin found.
Oregano: reported as glycoside; free-apigenin row verified:false.
